subject: Marketplace listing compliance & policy checks — branding, claims, SLAs
related_account: AWS Marketplace / Azure Marketplace / GCP Marketplace
messages:
From: Sophie Clark <sophie.clark@awsmarketplace.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing compliance: branding & SLAs

Hi Marissa / Camila,

Thanks for onboarding Redwood Inference to the AWS Marketplace pipeline. Before we can progress to co-sell enablement and publish, the Marketplace compliance team needs to confirm a few items related to your listing copy and claims. Quick checklist below — can you confirm by EOD Thursday?

- Branding assets: please confirm logo files (full-color, monochrome, 1:1 and horizontal) and any restricted marks. We need the asset pack and a signed brand usage attestation.
- Claims & product language: you currently reference "enterprise-grade SLA" and "99.9% uptime" in the draft. We require evidence/supporting language that defines measurement windows, exclusions, and applicable tiers (hosted vs dedicated/private).
- Support SLAs: clarify support hours (business hours vs 24x7), escalation matrix, and contact for critical incidents. Marketplace policy forbids "unlimited production support" claims without contractual backing.
- Co-sell prerequisites: please confirm whether you have an ISV Accelerate agreement and any reseller/partner channels you plan to list.

Attached: marketplace-compliance-checklist.pdf (form fields the team prefers you fill in).

If helpful, we can run a quick 30-min review with our compliance analyst — propose 3 slots tomorrow morning (10:00, 11:30, 14:00 PT).

Best,
Sophie Clark
Partner Compliance Manager, AWS Marketplace
Sophie.Clark@awsmarketplace.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing compliance: branding & SLAs

Hi Sophie — thanks for the checklist and the offer to review.

Quick answers and next steps from our side:
- Branding: attaching our asset pack and a brief brand usage attestation (see redwood-marketplace-responses.docx). We use the trade name "Redwood Inference" in legal contexts; public materials sometimes shorten to "Redwood" — noted if that needs tightening.
- Claims & language: we initially drafted "99.9% uptime" as a general claim for our Dedicated customers. We'll revise copy to specify scope (e.g., "99.9% monthly availability for Dedicated clusters, measured over rolling 30-day windows; exclusions apply — scheduled maintenance, force majeure, customer network issues"). Laura is on copy to finalize acceptable phrasing.
- Support SLAs: proposed matrix attached (support-sla-matrix.xlsx). High-level: Enterprise customers (Dedicated) get 24x7 priority support with 1-hour P1 response; Hosted/API tier gets business-hours support with 4-hour P1 response. We will not claim "unlimited production support" in public copy.
- Co-sell/isv: we are in the enrollment process for ISV Accelerate; can confirm on Thursday.

I'll book the 11:30 PT slot tomorrow for the compliance review unless you prefer another time.

Attachments: redwood-marketplace-responses.docx, support-sla-matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Clark <sophie.clark@awsmarketplace.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing compliance: branding & SLAs (legal notes)

Marissa / team — adding legal redlines and guidance. High-level comments below; see attached legal-redlines.pdf for line-by-line edits to the draft listing copy.

1) Uptime / SLA claims
- Do not publish bare numeric uptime claims without specifying measurement period and remedies. Suggested phrasing: "Targeted availability of 99.9% for Dedicated customers; see SLA in customer agreement for exclusions and remedies."
- If you wish to advertise an SLA-linked uptime publicly, the Marketplace requires a copy of the SLA and the terms referencing credits/penalties. We can publish the summary language but must link to the full SLA for customers.

2) Support language
- Remove or reword "unlimited production support." Instead use defined commitments (response times, escalation points).
- If you will offer 24x7 for certain tiers, ensure internal on-call rosters and runbook evidence exist; compliance may request proof during onboarding.

3) Trademark & branding
- Use the approved logo files only. Do not co-brand in a manner that implies AWS endorsement. The external teams will provide the AWS brand usage guidance; we should also include a one-line partner disclaimer on the listing.

4) Claims about data residency / privacy
- Any sentence about "data never leaves customer VPC" must be precise. If you offer a Private deployment, state it explicitly and avoid overbroad absolutes.

I'll be on the compliance call tomorrow.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Sophie Clark <sophie.clark@awsmarketplace.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing compliance: branding & SLAs — clarifications

Thanks for the quick responses — this is helpful. A few clarifications from marketplace side:

- Co-sell / ISV Accelerate: you should complete the ISV Accelerate registration before the co-sell badge can appear; the enrollment form is linked in our onboarding portal. If you need our ISV team to expedite, say so and I'll loop them in.
- Branding guide: AWS brand usage guidelines here: https://d1.awsstatic.com/partners/AWS_Partner_Branding_Guidelines.pdf — please use the specific full-color and mono logos for the marketplace tile.
- SLA claims: remove any public-facing statement that implies contractual credits unless you attach the SLA/MAA. You can state a measured target and link to the SLA doc.
- Support statements: Marketplace will flag "24/7 production support" unless backed by a support contract or service add-on. So the support-sla-matrix looks fine as internal guidance — but we need public copy to say "priority support available for Enterprise customers" and a link to support terms.

I removed one sentence from the draft that said "unlimited production support included" — that'll need to be updated. I've put a couple inline comments in the Doc you uploaded.

Next step: please upload the revised listing copy and a signed brand attestation to the portal. If you can get those to me by tomorrow EOD we can plan a compliance review with ISV Accelerate the following week.

Best,
Sophie

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Finalized marketplace copy & next steps

Sophie — thanks for the guidance and the call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching the revised marketplace copy and support matrix for your review: 20260318-marketplace-copy-v2.txt and support-sla-matrix.xlsx. Key edits summarized below: 

- Listing language now reads: "Targeted availability of 99.9% for Dedicated clusters (measured monthly). See full SLA for exclusions and remedies."
- Support language now: "Priority support available for Enterprise (Dedicated) customers; standard support available during business hours for Hosted API customers. See full support terms."
- Removed all references to "unlimited production support."
- Trademark usage updated to use "Redwood Inference" in the title and full-color logo in the tile.

Action items: 
- Sophie: please confirm whether the revised language satisfies Marketplace compliance. If yes, we'll upload the signed brand attestation and SLA docs to the portal and request ISV Accelerate enrollment.
- Camila / Jonas: prepare co-sell collateral (one-pager + deal registration template) once Sophie confirms listing approval.
- Laura: please confirm the SLA summary is acceptable for the public listing and we can provide the full SLA to Marketplace under NDA.

Tentative publish window: two weeks from today, pending sign-offs. If anything else is required for Azure or GCP listings, we can parallelize the edits — cc'd their contacts earlier in the thread.

Thanks all — ping me for a quick sync if we need to escalate.

Marissa Cole
